name: EU AI Act: high-risk readiness / 高风险准备度 (draft)
description: Selected provider-side readiness evidence for Articles 9, 11 and 14. Available before application deadlines; gaps are preparation gaps, not findings of an applicable legal violation.
limitations: Unreviewed preparation checklist, not full AI Act coverage, conformity assessment, CE marking or deployment approval.

The Commission timeline checked on 2026-11-13 lists Annex III high-risk rules for 2027-12-02 and Annex I product high-risk rules for 2028-08-02. Individual transitional provisions require legal review.
No effective_from is set deliberately: this is readiness assessment, not an assertion that future obligations already apply.
Scope is an assessment assertion, not verified classification. A false scope routes substantive controls out but never passes the unconditional scope review.

Document and assessment booleans only describe submitted evidence. GovWeave does not read documents or verify their adequacy. The 30-day freshness limit is a local assurance choice, not a statutory deadline.
Excludes full data governance, quality management, registration, post-market obligations, deployer duties, prohibited practices and GPAI. Human oversight and legal classification remain manual.

controls.title: Review provider scope and applicable dates
controls.remediation: Record role, Annex classification, exemptions, transitional dates and the rationale for scope.euhr_in_scope.

controls.title: Risk-management record available
controls.remediation: Supply a version-linked risk register covering intended use and foreseeable misuse.

controls.title: Pre-market test evidence available
controls.remediation: Reference tests and predefined metrics for this version; evidence availability is not test adequacy or success.

controls.title: Technical documentation available
controls.remediation: Reference maintained technical documentation; arrange separate Annex IV completeness review.

controls.title: Review effective human oversight
controls.remediation: Review whether responsible people can understand limitations, intervene and stop operation safely.
